summary: Defines Management Information Base objects for managing the Traffic Engineering Database used with MPLS-TE and GMPLS. Network management systems can then read this database via standard management protocols such as SNMP.

eli5.summary: A router's notebook of which roads have spare room is given a standard window, so a manager can look in and read it.

subtitle: A standard SNMP window onto the link topology database that MPLS-TE and GMPLS routers build from OSPF and IS-IS.

tldr.problem: Existing OSPF, IS-IS, MPLS and GMPLS MIBs give network managers no way to retrieve the topology information of MPLS and GMPLS networks.
tldr.mechanism: The TED-MIB module defines five tables (tedTable, tedLocalIfAddrTable, tedRemoteIfAddrTable, tedSwCapTable, tedSrlgTable) and three notifications that mirror the TE link data carried in OSPF-TE and IS-IS-TE.
tldr.outcome: A management system can poll the tables and be notified when entries change. Nearly everything is read-only, and IANA assigned the module number 273.

today: RFC 6825 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata shows it has not been obsoleted or updated by another RFC.

sections.title: Why a TED MIB
sections.content:
MPLS and GMPLS traffic engineering extend the OSPF and IS-IS routing protocols with extra link information. Routers collect this into a Traffic Engineering Database (TED). A MIB (Management Information Base) is a set of objects that is normally read over SNMP, and the OSPF, IS-IS, MPLS and GMPLS MIBs already exist. But the RFC states that they do not offer a management interface to retrieve the topology information of MPLS and GMPLS networks.

This memo fills that gap with a MIB module written in SMIv2. It is meant to be used alongside the OSPFv2, OSPFv3 and IS-IS MIBs and the MPLS/GMPLS TE MIBs, so that a management system can see routing information and LSP information together. It can also be implemented alone, for instance when the management system only needs TE link topology.
sections.eli5: Routers keep a private list of which roads between them have room. This RFC gives the list a standard front door, so any manager program can read it the same way on any brand of router.

sections.title: The Five Tables
sections.content:
The module follows the shape of the TE sub-TLVs inside a Link TLV. Anything that can appear more than once for the same link gets its own table.

  • tedTable holds the core TED data from OSPF-TE or IS-IS-TE. It leaves out the interface addresses, switching capability descriptor and shared risk link group data.
  • tedLocalIfAddrTable and tedRemoteIfAddrTable hold the local and remote interface IP addresses. They are separate because the Interface IP Address sub-TLV may appear more than once with the same Link-TLV.
  • tedSwCapTable holds the Interface Switching Capability Descriptor information, again separate because it can repeat.
  • tedSrlgTable holds Shared Risk Link Group information, for the same reason.

When the information comes from a plain MPLS network, the four GMPLS-specific tables are not supported.
sections.eli5: There is one main table for the basics of each link and four small side tables. The side tables exist because a link can have several of those extra details, and one table row cannot hold a list.

sections.title: What tedTable Records
sections.content:
Each row in tedTable describes one TE link. It is indexed by four objects: tedLocalRouterId, tedRemoteRouterId, tedLinkInformationSource and tedLinkIndex. The source says where the data came from: unknown(0), locallyConfigured(1), ospfv2(2), ospfv3(3), isis(4) or other(5). Router and link identifiers mean OSPF or IS-IS identifiers depending on the source, and a locally configured link uses a locally defined value.

Read-only columns include the link state (unknown, up, down), the IGP area, the link type (pointToPoint or multiAccess), the TE router ID and link ID addresses, the TE metric, the maximum and maximum reservable bandwidth, unreserved bandwidth at priorities 0 to 7, the administrative group, the local and remote identifiers of an unnumbered link, and the link protection type.

Bandwidth values use the Float32TC type from RFC 6340 and are given in bytes per second. The tedLinkInformationData object can point to the matching row in another MIB, such as the TE link MIB of RFC 4220, or hold zeroDotZero.
sections.eli5: Each row is a card about one road between two routers. It says who is at each end, whether the road is open, how wide it is and how much room is still free.

sections.title: Polling and Notifications
sections.content:
A management system is expected to retrieve the tables periodically to understand the detailed topology. The module is limited to read-only access, with two exceptions: tedStatusChangeNotificationMaxRate and tedCreatedDeletedNotificationMaxRate. Each limits how many notifications are generated per minute, with a default of 1. For the status-change rate, a value of 0 means no throttling.

The RFC says plainly that the module has no functionality to notify network failures as such. It does notify topology changes with three notifications: tedStatusChange, tedEntryCreated and tedEntryDeleted. For example, a status change should be generated when unreserved bandwidth changes in a way that creates or deletes an LSP over the TE link.

The module is designed to be independent of the OSPF and IS-IS MIBs, although each TE link belongs to a node or link managed by the routing protocol. The RFC walks through an example of a numbered TE link on a GMPLS node: a point-to-point link that is up, with TE router ID 192.0.2.1, link ID 192.0.2.10, a metric of 1, and a switching capability of lsc(150) with ethernet(2) encoding.
sections.eli5: A manager can look at the notebook every so often, or get a note when something changes. A limit on how many notes per minute keeps a busy router from shouting too much.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Even readable objects can be sensitive, because the five tables reveal the topology of the MPLS/GMPLS network. An operator who does not want that revealed should control GET and NOTIFY access, and possibly encrypt the values when they travel over SNMP.

The only writable objects are the two notification maximum-rate objects. Malicious changes could overload the management agent, the network or the router with notifications when the network is changing a lot.

SNMP versions before SNMPv3 did not include adequate security. Implementations MUST provide the SNMPv3 security features, including authentication and privacy via the User-based Security Model with AES, and MAY support the Transport Security Model with a secure transport such as SSH or TLS/DTLS. Deploying SNMP versions before SNMPv3 is NOT RECOMMENDED. Operators remain responsible for giving access only to legitimate principals.
sections.eli5: The notebook shows how a network is wired, which is private. So only trusted managers should be allowed to read it, and their conversations should be locked.

sections.title: IANA Assignment
sections.content: IANA assigned the value 273 to the TED-MIB module in the Internet-standard MIB Transmission Group registry, so the module sits at transmission 273. New assignments there require Specification Required. IANA also marked 273 as Reserved in the ifType definitions registry.
sections.eli5: The module was given its own number, 273, in an official list, so nobody else reuses it.
